think_procedure: 1) Identify the knob’s data type and allowed values in PostgreSQL. 2) Check whether it is a numeric knob with an inherent ordering (e.g., integer/float range). 3) If numeric, look for sentinel/special values (commonly -1, 0) that change semantics (e.g., disable/auto) rather than just adjusting magnitude. 4) If the knob is boolean or enum (non-numeric), it does not fit the ‘special numerical knob’ pattern described. 5) Conclude whether it is a special knob and, if so, record the special value(s).
